title: Female borrowers using standardized narrative templates for goals and gratitude may exhibit different funding speeds.
Female borrowers who provide a specific seasonal timeline for business operations may fund faster.
Female borrowers who emphasize general improvement of children's lives or skills may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who use standardized location-based greetings may fund faster.
Female borrowers who specify a business duration of two years or more may fund faster.
Female borrowers who explicitly mention prior loan repayment history may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention the length of time their business has operated may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention a history of previous loan repayment may fund faster.
Female borrowers whose loan requests are for furniture items may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who express direct gratitude to lenders may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that include specific monthly income figures predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Borrowers who explicitly name their institutional partner fund faster regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention family members or household responsibilities fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention specific agricultural inputs fund faster.
